title: When the Landfall Turns
premise: Riverboat captain Wren Galloway is hired to resupply a survey expedition that has gone silent in the flooded headwaters of the Serrano River. What they find is not disaster but discovery: the expedition has located an ancient river-civilization's drowned archive, and its leader, Dr. Imara Voss, intends to claim it for her backers by any means necessary. As the monsoon season closes in, Wren must choose between loyalty to their found crew, obedience to the contract, and the truth about what the water remembers. The story ends with Voss's expedition broken apart, the archive's location deliberately lost to the rising flood, and Wren bringing home only the people — having learned that belonging cannot be charted like miles.
about_author: Wren Halloran spent six seasons working deckhand jobs on inland waterways before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on a lifelong fascination with rivers as places where maps fail and people are revealed.

chapters.title: Soundings
chapters.summary: Wren Galloway pilots the Marguerite through low-water season, establishing their intimate knowledge of the river and their crew: engineer Odile, deckhand Tam, and cook Bex. A telegram arrives offering triple pay for an emergency run upriver. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness — ten years of miles instead of years.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: In Port Calloway, Wren meets Dr. Imara Voss, who offers a lucrative contract to resupply and retrieve the Halcyon Survey team, silent for three weeks. The terms include a secrecy clause that makes Wren uneasy. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: temptation versus instinct; the money could buy the Marguerite outright.

chapters.title: Upriver Traffic
chapters.summary: The crew debates taking the job; Tam warns about monsoon timing, Odile about the engine's age. They cast off anyway, passing refugee barges heading downriver who report strange lights upstream. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: the crew's banter revealing they are already a family, even if no one says it.

chapters.title: First Silence
chapters.summary: At the last radio relay station, the operator admits the Survey's frequency went quiet after reporting 'a find.' That night someone searches the Marguerite's cargo hold. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: creeping dread; the river feels watched, and Wren realizes Voss brought more than science aboard.

chapters.title: The Drowned Terraces
chapters.summary: High water reveals stone terraces usually submerged — carvings too regular to be natural. Voss grows secretive, consulting privately with her security chief, Mercer. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion as Wren recognizes Voss cares nothing for the river itself.

chapters.title: Answer at Last
chapters.summary: The Marguerite reaches the Survey camp: intact but fortified, half the scientists gone, the rest exhausted and frightened. Lead geologist Ansel Reyes begs them to leave before explaining why. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: relief at contact shadowed by the realization that rescue may be a cover story.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel shows Wren the discovery: a cavern system beneath the terraces holding a preserved archive of a river civilization — records, tools, art. Voss wants it extracted and sold. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: wonder and grief; the archive belongs to the river's living descendants, not to backers.

chapters.title: Mercer's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mercer begins inventorying the archive for removal, intimidating the remaining scientists. Tam catches him falsifying the radio log to hide their position from downstream authorities. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: anger hardening into resolve; the crew quietly aligns against Voss.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile calculates they have nine days before landfall makes the return run impossible. Voss orders the Marguerite held at the camp 'for safety' — effectively seizing the boat. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the river that defines Wren is being taken away.

chapters.title: Downstream Kin
chapters.summary: A small boat arrives carrying elders from river settlements — descendants of the archive's makers, drawn by dreams and rumor. Voss turns them away; Wren secretly meets with their speaker, Mama Ilo. POV: Mama Ilo. Emotional beat: recognition; Wren sees belonging modeled as stewardship, not ownership.

chapters.title: Split Cargo
chapters.summary: Voss offers Wren a fortune to ferry the first load of artifacts out ahead of the storm. Wren stalls, buying time while Ansel documents everything. Mercer grows violent with a junior scientist. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — the bribe would solve every problem except conscience.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone cripples the Survey's generator; Voss blames the crew and confines them. Bex discovers Mercer's real orders: extract the archive and burn the site to erase evidence of the backers' involvement. POV: Bex. Emotional beat: fear becoming fury; the stakes shift from profit to erasure.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Wren, Tam, and Ansel slip out to move the Survey's wounded scientist to the elders' settlement, navigating flooded channels by memory and starlight. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grace under pressure; the river, which Voss treats as obstacle, becomes ally.

chapters.title: Mama Ilo's Bargain
chapters.summary: At the settlement, Mama Ilo agrees to shelter the scientists but asks Wren to ensure the archive stays with the water. Wren promises nothing yet, torn between promise-keeping and survival. POV: Mama Ilo. Emotional beat: weight of trust extended without guarantee.

chapters.title: Landfall Warning
chapters.summary: The storm shifts course — five days, not nine. Voss accelerates loading, forcing scientists to haul crates at gunpoint. Odile covertly weakens the crane rigging. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: ticking-clock tension; sabotage as quiet resistance.

chapters.title: The Crane Falls
chapters.summary: The rigged crane collapses, destroying half the packed crates and injuring Mercer. Voss accuses Wren outright and holds the crew at gunpoint on the Marguerite's deck as the sky darkens. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: open rupture; pretense of legality gone, only power remains.

chapters.title: Mutiny at the Mooring
chapters.summary: Ansel and the scientists refuse to load further. In the standoff, Wren cuts the Marguerite loose from Voss's control, and the crew takes the boat — leaving Voss and Mercer ashore with a radio and tents. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: costly courage; choosing people over contract.

chapters.title: Running Ahead of the Rain
chapters.summary: Descent through rising water: sandbars moved, channels drowned, the Marguerite pushed to her limits. They ferry the scientists and as many of Mama Ilo's people as fit, leaving the archive sealed behind them. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: exhilaration and grief entwined; saving what can be saved.

chapters.title: Voss's Last Radio
chapters.summary: Voss broadcasts threats and then pleas; Wren answers once, telling her the river will decide. At the narrows, the Marguerite threads a channel only Wren knows, losing their pursuers' chartered launch behind them. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph; mercy offered to someone who wouldn't give it.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits as they reach the delta settlement. Together with the elders, they weather the storm, the boat lashed and singing. Voss's fate upstream remains unknown; the backers' names go into Ansel's sealed report. POV: Bex. Emotional beat: communal endurance; found family tested and holding.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Weeks later, an inquiry convenes. Wren testifies to the seizure and the danger, saying nothing of the archive's contents or location — honoring both law and promise. The backers retreat; Ansel's report protects the site. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet integrity; some truths belong to the water.

chapters.title: Miles, Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Spring season opens. The Marguerite runs again with a fuller crew — Ansel aboard, Mama Ilo's grandchildren visiting the wheelhouse. Wren still measures life in miles, but now the miles lead somewhere. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the river as home rather than escape.
